metadata.description: Reusable motion and interaction patterns that can supplement the separate visual-style catalog.
metadata.interpretation_note: The supplied reference images show titles rather than complete motion sequences. These entries propose adaptable interpretations; they do not claim to reproduce an observed original animation or its toolchain.

fable_opening_review.method: 8 fps chronological frame inspection of first three seconds; not continuous playback or audio review

selection_policy: Motion patterns are optional additions to a style, not replacements for its existing motion direction. The style visual_cues, technique, typography, material behavior, and topic take precedence. Select only patterns that clarify the scene; choosing none is valid. Resolve conflicts by adapting or omitting the pattern rather than weakening the style. Treat timing, intensity, and audio suggestions as adjustable creative parameters.
render_contract: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method. Visual and motion layers expose deterministic state at composition time, or supply baked assets or frame sequences. The pipeline supplies seekable time and composes their output. Timeline registration and frame hooks are integration adapters, not substitutes for style-specific rendering or motion. Use HyperFrames first and Remotion only under the style catalog fallback condition. For video, replace live hover, scroll, or pointer input with explicit keyframed progress and an authored pointer path when needed. Compute the visible state directly from composition time; seeking to the same time must produce the same frame regardless of playback history. Do not depend on real pointer events, browser scroll state, wall clocks, uncontrolled loops, or accumulated particle history during rendering. Let the selected framework own playback. Preserve local-font loading, seeded randomness, and cached simulations. For HyperFrames Canvas or WebGL layers, register a paused GSAP timeline and a deterministic renderAt(time) function. Handle hf-seek to synchronize state and repaint even when GSAP callbacks are suppressed; invoke the same renderer during normal timeline updates. Avoid duplicate seek listeners and clean them up when the composition is disposed. In another framework, use its documented frame or seek mechanism rather than HyperFrames globals.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

patterns.name: Hover-Triggered Door Bloom Interaction
patterns.description: A hover reveal in which a hinged door opens and flowers emerge from the opening. Leaving the hover region reverses both actions from their current progress, rather than resetting the scene. Opening and blooming share one reversible sequence.
motion_sequence: Establish the closed door and the space from which the flowers will emerge.
On hover, swing the door open while revealing and moving the flowers outward in a coordinated sequence.
Keep the open, blooming state while hover remains active. On hover exit, retrace the sequence from its current position until the flowers withdraw and the door closes.

interaction.progress_driver: Drive one bounded sequence toward its open end on hover and toward its closed end on hover exit. Reverse from the current playhead position, including during an incomplete opening. Define equivalent focus or tap controls for interactive delivery.
interaction.exit_behavior: Reverse the door and flower sequence continuously from the current state. Do not snap closed, restart the closing animation from fully open, or leave the flowers behind.

patterns.video_adaptation: Schedule approach, opening and bloom, hold, and withdrawal on the video timeline. Include a partial-opening reversal if demonstrating interruption. Derive both the hinge pose and flower state from the same authored progress; live hover events must not be required.

Use motion/react only within mounted React components.

tech.implementation: Use a hinged DOM or SVG layer, layered cutouts, or true 3D door geometry. Reveal and move authored flower layers from the opening with controlled masks and depth order. Bind the hinge and flower transforms to one paused, reversible sequence. For video, evaluate authored opening or closing progress directly from composition time; do not depend on a hover handler to establish state.
tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

The opening hero fades, surrounding bands expand beyond the frame edges, and the dark central opening grows to cover the view before revealing the next chapter. The main action is camera passage between scenes, not simply spinning a decorative spiral.
motion_sequence: Establish the opening hero and the central tunnel entrance.

interaction.progress_driver: Map a finite scroll range to normalized transit progress for interactive output.

patterns.video_adaptation: Replace scroll progress with a keyed progress parameter over a chosen scene interval. Use a camera path or spiral transform that can be evaluated at any progress value. Provide readable entrance and exit states.

patterns.name: Immersive Float
patterns.description: An orb hovers above a soft form. Activation makes the orb fall and compress on contact; a growth front then spreads across the receiving surface from the impact point. Small sparks and flowers accompany the expanding front. The central action is a triggered drop, impact, and spreading transformation, rather than unrelated layers drifting.

On click or equivalent activation, drop the orb and show a squash at contact.
Begin surface growth at the impact point and expand it across the form, with small sparks and flowers following the growth boundary.
Hold the transformed surface so the result of the action remains readable.

interaction.progress_driver: Activation starts an ordered drop, contact compression, and surface-growth sequence. Keep the pre-activation hover distinct from the triggered transformation.
interaction.exit_behavior: Pointer exit does not undo the transformation. Retain the completed state; replay or reset is an optional designed control, not an assumed behavior.

patterns.name: Scroll-Driven Helix Flow
patterns.description: A continuous camera move follows a luminous double helix through three presentation stages: a wide establishing view, a close view of individual rungs, and a wide view from the other side. Copy changes at these stages. The defining motion is a guided viewpoint journey along the structure, rather than particles or cards advancing around it.
motion_sequence: Establish the double helix in a wide view with the first copy state.
Dolly along the structure toward a close view that makes individual rungs readable, then change the copy for that stage.
Continue to a wide view from the other side, change to the final copy state, and provide a reading hold.

interaction.progress_driver: Map a bounded scroll range to a continuous camera path with wide, close, and opposite-side wide stages. Derive the copy windows from the same progress.
interaction.exit_behavior: Reverse through the camera path and copy windows continuously when scrolling backward; hold endpoint states outside the bounded range.

patterns.video_adaptation: Replace scrolling with keyed camera-path progress. Evaluate camera pose and stage-specific copy from the same composition time. Preserve the wide-to-close-to-opposite-wide progression; video export must not depend on live scroll input.

patterns.description: A glowing doorway anchors a horizon scene. The scene slowly advances toward the viewer, mist rises from the ground, and pointer movement offsets or tilts depth layers to create parallax. The doorway remains the focal destination; this is not a light trail following the cursor.
motion_sequence: Establish the luminous doorway, horizon, ground, depth layers, and a stable focal destination.
Gradually advance the scene toward the viewer while mist rises from the ground.
Superimpose bounded pointer-driven depth-layer offsets or tilts without losing the doorway anchor.
Maintain a readable atmospheric composition; passage through the doorway is an optional extension rather than a required ending.

interaction.progress_driver: Use scene time for the slow advance and rising mist. Use normalized pointer coordinates for bounded depth-dependent layer offsets or tilts. Keep these two drivers distinct.
interaction.exit_behavior: Settle pointer-dependent parallax toward a neutral pose on exit while retaining the scheduled scene advance. Do not invent a cursor light trail.

patterns.video_adaptation: Schedule the scene advance and evaluate rising mist from deterministic time or cached animation. Author a pointer target path only if a parallax response is needed; a visible cursor is optional. Render layer offsets from that path and time without live pointer input or accumulated mist history.

patterns.name: Lighting State Progression
patterns.description: Keep one environment and its spatial anchors recognizable while coordinated lighting states advance the story. Sky, landscape, reflections and state-owned light accents change coherently; subjects retain their material identity. An authored cloud or shadow front can reveal the next state.
motion_sequence: Establish the fixed stage and hero in the first lighting state and hold.
Bring an in-world wipe mass (cloud, smoke, shadow or light front) across the frame.
Recolor all environment layers to the next lighting state behind the wipe edge, swapping celestial props, while the hero's color stays constant.
Clear the wipe and hold the new state; let the hero react or act on its own cue.
Repeat for further states, ending on a settled lit state.

Coordinate celestial props, local reflections, shadows and emissive details with the new state. Preserve object base materials while allowing consistent illumination. A deterministic masked cloud/shadow-front handoff is an optional implementation adaptation: the one-second source samples do not establish its exact timing or masking method. Hold each state before advancing and settle the final state.

patterns.name: 360° Camera Orbit (360度环绕运镜)
patterns.description: The camera makes one full 360-degree circuit around a stationary hero, timed by absolute composition time, with a held opening view and a held ending view. The camera is the only thing that moves.
motion_sequence: Opening hold: show the stationary {{subject}} from the starting view θ0, with target, horizon, ground contact, key light and world landmarks fixed. Hold long enough for the viewer to read the hero and its surroundings.
Ease in: progress starts from zero velocity. The camera begins moving along a fixed radius and height circle while camera.lookAt stays on the fixed target. The subject does not rotate.

Full circuit: θ = θ0 + direction·2π·progress sweeps through side, rear and opposite-side views. Parallax between the hero and world landmarks, occlusion changes and fixed shadow directions show that the camera is moving, not the subject.
Ease out: progress settles to exactly 1 as the camera returns to θ0 + direction·2π, which is the same pose as the opening view.
Ending hold: keep the returned front view still. Any closing title or label is revealed only after the camera has stopped and is held long enough to read.
patterns.video_adaptation: Write camera pose as a pure function of absolute composition time t, then render. tOrbit = clamp((t − openHold) / orbitDuration, 0, 1). progress = ease(tOrbit), using a symmetric ease-in-out such as sine or power2, or linear for a mechanical turntable feel. θ = θ0 + direction·2π·progress. Position comes from the fixed radius r and height h around the fixed target, followed by lookAt(target) with a constant up vector. Do not integrate per frame, damp, use requestAnimationFrame, timers, OrbitControls, pointer, scroll or wall-clock state. Direct seeks forward, backward and to a fresh page must give identical frames. When t ≥ openHold + orbitDuration, the frame equals the opening view, so the ending hold is a true return. Choose orbit duration from subject complexity and what the viewer must notice. Large travel needs enough time to read rear details without strobing or motion smear. Short clips may hold less, but never cut the circuit short silently. If a shorter arc (for example 90° or 180°) is chosen, label it 'partial arc adaptation'. For a captured turntable, index frames by θ only at captured angles, and state how many views exist and how the background and lighting behave (a physical turntable rotates the subject against fixed lights, which differs from a camera orbit). Optional text belongs to a screen-space layer timed to the holds. Container-owned labels follow data-reveal-after rules. Any arrow hides its head until the shaft completes.

suggested_libraries.name: Three.js
suggested_libraries.purpose: Render genuine 3D forms or shader treatments when a 2D solution is insufficient.

tech.implementation: Choose the renderer route by asset capability. (1) Genuine 3D: in a Three.js scene, the hero group's transform is never animated by this preset. A PerspectiveCamera with constant FOV, or an OrthographicCamera when the Motion Graphic needs orthographic but not strict isometric framing, sits on a circle of radius r at height h around a fixed Vector3 target. On every seek, call setCameraForTime(t): compute θ, set camera.position, call camera.lookAt(target), then renderer.render(scene, camera) synchronously. Lights, shadow cameras, environment maps, ground and landmarks are world-space and do not follow the camera unless the brief asks for a camera-attached rim light, which must be disclosed. Check that rear and underside surfaces seen from height h are finished, with no open meshes, missing backfaces or unpainted UV areas. Fit radius so the silhouette stays inside safe margins at every θ. Check near and far planes so nothing clips. (2) Prerendered: an offline 3D render, such as Blender, with the same camera-math path can be baked to an image sequence and indexed by frame from time. (3) Captured turntable: index real photographs by angle and state the coverage. Do not interpolate unseen angles or invent back views. Screen-space labels can reproject anchors with Vector3.project on each seek. Stay inside the selected Motion Graphic's palette and medium. Do not add perspective orbit to flat posters, diagrams, strict isometric treatments or print typography. Anatomy's isometric kit is not used for this preset because the motion needs a free camera, not fixed isometric axes.
tech.library_selection: style_renderer: Three.js (PerspectiveCamera or OrthographicCamera, Group, Vector3, WebGLRenderer) for genuine 3D, or a prerendered sequence from an available offline 3D tool. Report any missing tool rather than substituting one. motion_engine: a pure time-to-θ function. GSAP may supply easing only (gsap.parseEase or a paused timeline with a proxy progress value that one owner writes to the camera). Never require live OrbitControls, ScrollTrigger, pointer input, timers or autonomous loops for video. Give each animated property one owner: the camera pose belongs only to this preset, and the hero transform is not animated by it. Composition and export follow the requested pipeline: Use the project's selected Multiplane, HyperFrames or Remotion renderer. Multiplane hosts genuine Three.js scenes through Shot.define.render(t), or a prerendered layer. Multiplane's layered planes alone give only bounded parallax, which must be labelled as a partial arc adaptation, not a 360° orbit. The pipeline does not decide whether real 3D exists.

motion_engine.selection_basis: A pure composition-time camera function owns the pose; GSAP easing is optional.

patterns.name: Glyph Ink-Flood Container Handoff
patterns.description: A settled title becomes the next scene's container. Ink floods the glyph counters and gaps, starting from the centre glyphs and spreading outward, until the word fuses into one solid block whose ragged rim still traces the outer letter silhouettes. The block is recoloured to the container hue, grows into a background panel, and the incoming title writes on inside the completed panel.
motion_sequence: Hold the readable outgoing title in its frame for a full reading hold.
Dilate each glyph's ink from a chosen seed (centre glyphs first) so counters and inter-glyph gaps close quickly, keeping the outer silhouette ragged.
Lock the merged block with no holes, recolour it to the incoming container hue, and expand its bounds to the panel rectangle while the ragged rim relaxes.
Write on the incoming title inside the completed panel and hold it for reading.
patterns.video_adaptation: Compute every glyph's dilation radius from absolute composition time, ordered by distance from the seed glyph. Use a morphological dilation of the real glyph shapes (SVG feMorphology dilate, a Canvas round-joined text stroke, or an SDF threshold), never a generic opaque rectangle wipe. Once every glyph has fully dilated, fill the block's core so no counter survives; roughen the rim with fixed seeded offsets so it never boils during holds. Interpolate the block's bounds to the panel rectangle after the merge and crossfade only the fill colour. Mark the incoming title data-reveal-after the panel so it stays hidden until the container is complete. Bracket or frame ornaments outside the word stay fixed.

patterns.name: Annotation-Mark Portal Transition
patterns.description: A hand-drawn annotation changes role and becomes the portal into the next section. A marker stroke leaves a connector, closes a rounded lasso around a region and holds; the same stroke then straightens into a rectangle that re-crops the lassoed content, scales it toward the camera and locks as the empty border of the next section, whose ornaments and title appear inside it. A highlighter bar that scales past the card and is torn away is a secondary form.
motion_sequence: Settle the outgoing layout, then draw the annotation stroke along its authored path in reading order.
Hold the closed annotation so the viewer registers the selected region.
Morph the same stroke from rounded lasso to rectangle (matched points) while its clipped contents scale toward the camera about the region's centre.
Lock the frame at its final screen rectangle, clear the old scene, and reveal the next section's ornaments and content inside the completed frame.
patterns.video_adaptation: Author the lasso and the target rectangle with the same point count and draw the stroke with a time-driven dash window. Keep the frame stroke as one persistent element from the first draw to the final border; never swap in a new rectangle. Use the current shape (lasso, then rectangle) as the clip for a copy of the region's content, and interpolate its transform about the region centroid from absolute composition time. An optional directional blur belongs only to the two or three peak frames. Mark the incoming title and ornaments data-reveal-after the frame. For the highlighter form, scale the bar rect to the viewport, then run a seeded torn-edge (or slide-off) wipe.

tech.implementation: Precompute the lasso (with a fixed hand wobble) and its rectangle counterpart at identical parameter values. Draw the stroke by arc length from absolute time; after the hold, interpolate wobble to zero and lasso to rectangle, collapse the connector tail onto the loop start, and interpolate the frame box from the lasso bounds to the final rect while clipping the region copy. Scale that copy uniformly (cover, centred on the region) so it crops rather than stretches. Resample lasso and rectangle by perimeter with the four corners as exact samples, so the locked frame is a true rectangle with the same point count. Keep one stroke element throughout. Reveal ornaments and title only after the frame has locked. The explorer preview is a Canvas 2D schematic, not the source video or a prescribed production renderer.

adapt_or_omit_when: Use when an annotation already points at the region the next section is about.
Omit when the annotation must remain as a note, or when the next section has nothing to do with the marked region.
A portal zoom without a drawn mark, or a mark that is swapped for a new rectangle, does not demonstrate this pattern.

patterns.name: Cumulative Device-Feed Pipeline
patterns.description: An input→machine→output explainer built around one persistent hero device. A pointer clicks the device awake. Each numbered step card slides in, builds its content only after the card is complete, draws a feed arrow and docks into the device as a reduced chip that stays visible. A pull-back fans every chip at the side with feed arrows, the device shows processing (nodes before connectors), and its screen bursts past the bezel into an output window whose contents fill in after it settles.
motion_sequence: Establish the hero device at a fixed anchor; optional activation beat (pointer arrives, screen state switches).
For each step: slide in the card, reveal its heading and content after the card is complete, and draw a feed arrow whose head appears only when the shaft reaches the device.
Absorb the finished card toward the device screen as a reduced chip while the next card enters; earlier chips are never removed.

After the last input, pull back to show all reduced chips with feed arrows, then show processing on the screen with nodes before connectors, and hold the completed diagram long enough to read before the output.
Burst the screen fill beyond the bezel into the output container, reveal its contents after it settles, and hold for reading.
patterns.video_adaptation: Model the scene as data: device rect, screen rect, step cards with content items, arrow paths and the output window. Compute every element's transform and visibility from absolute composition time with per-step windows (enter, build, arrow, absorb, persist). Reduced chips use deterministic dock and fan targets and remain visible through the output. Draw arrows with a time-driven dash and a separate head annotated data-arrowhead-for, shown only at full shaft progress in every seek direction. End every feed arrow on free device edge that no docked chip covers, keep the head outside the target, and give dark arrows a light keyline where they cross dark areas. Grow processing nodes before their connectors, build the output burst from fixed seeded ray geometry and a halftone pattern, and reveal output contents data-reveal-after the window. Supply an original device illustration; label any fictional interface as illustrative.

suggested_libraries.name: GSAP
suggested_libraries.purpose: Create a paused, seekable timeline for progress, transforms, masks, and controlled easing.

tech.implementation: Lay out the device, screen, cards, dock and fan targets and the output window as constants. For each step compute rest, dock and fan rects from absolute time; reveal card contents only after its entrance completes; draw feed arrows with hidden heads until complete. During processing, show a node only after its pop and a connector only after both endpoint nodes exist. Grow the output window from the screen rect with seeded spikes and halftone dots, then reveal its contents. The explorer preview is a Canvas 2D schematic with an original code-drawn device, not the source video or a prescribed production renderer.

adapt_or_omit_when: Use when a process genuinely takes several inputs into one tool or machine and produces an output the viewer should see.
Omit for a single-step action or when no meaningful output exists; card stacking or a data build alone may be clearer.
Any interface shown in the output must be accurate for the real product or labelled illustrative.

patterns.audio_direction_prompt: Suggest audio from the actual brief and scene. No audio was analysed in the source frame review; restrained clicks at activation and absorption and one accent at the output burst are optional, and previews stay silent.
patterns.executable_prompt_template: Build Cumulative Device-Feed Pipeline (motion-046) for {{subject}} in {{visual_style}}. Keep one hero device fixed and drawn from original or authorised assets. Activate it with a pointer beat, then for each step slide in a card, reveal its labels only after the card is complete, draw a feed arrow whose head appears only once the shaft reaches the device, and absorb the card into the device as a reduced chip that stays visible. After the last input, pull back to show every chip with feed arrows, show processing with nodes before connectors, then burst the screen into the output window and reveal its contents after it settles. Compute every transform from absolute composition time; use fixed seeded burst geometry. Resolve {{motion_parameters}} (steps, holds, dock/fan targets, burst). Preserve the selected Motion Graphic's palette and medium and label fictional interfaces illustrative. Verify forward, backward and direct seeks. Use {{render_pipeline}} for composition timing, synchronization, validation and export; preserve the selected style renderer and motion ownership.
verification: Each card's labels are hidden until the card's container is complete.
Arrowheads stay hidden until their shafts reach the endpoint, in forward, backward and direct seeks.
Earlier input chips remain visible and stable after absorption, through to the output.
Flowchart connectors never appear before both endpoint nodes, and the completed diagram holds (about 0.4–0.5 s in the preview) before the burst covers it.
No arrowhead or arrow endpoint is hidden under a docked chip or another card.
Seeking to any time, including from a fresh page, reproduces identical frames; the step order is readable, with holds sized to the copy.
patterns.palette_guidance: This pattern adds no required colors. Keep the device's material colors constant, give each step card a distinct but related surface, keep arrows in one high-contrast ink, and reserve one accent for the output burst. The preview uses an illustrative deep-teal ground with static wedges, a grey code-drawn device, paper-white and mustard cards, near-black arrows and a coral accent; these are not binding.

source_evidence.source_file: User-supplied recording: motion-graphics intro of a Bilibili tutorial (watermark 在下鱼酥), 910×512, 30 fps, 60 s
source_evidence.sampling: Six Opus 5.5 batches inspected all 1,800 thumbnails and contact sheets; the consolidation pass read frames 1672 and 1733 at full resolution and this implementation pass read frames 1672, 1700, 1733, 1737 and 1744. No continuous playback or audio analysis.

observations.observation: Card ① builds its heading, wireframe blocks and image chips, then shrinks into the screen while card ② arrives; the reduced ① chip sits partly inside the screen.
After a pull-back, ① and ② are fanned at the left with arrows into the device, the ③ headline lands and a flowchart grows on the screen node by node.
The screen fill bursts past the bezel with radial halftone rays while the earlier cards are still visible, and settles into a centred output window whose image and UI bars fill in.

limitations: Arrowhead-versus-shaft timing in the source could not be confirmed; the endpoint rule is applied rather than copied.
The photoreal CRT and source UI are non-reusable assets; the preview uses an original code-drawn device.
Exact easing and whether the pull-back is a camera move or a group scale are not determinable from stills; the preview moves chips to fan targets.

library_options.name: Three.js
library_options.purpose: Build 3D scenes, cameras, geometry, materials, lighting, and shader effects.
library_options.integration_guidance: Derive scene state from composition time and render explicitly. Do not run an independent animation loop during video export.

library_options.name: PixiJS
library_options.purpose: Render layered sprites, vector graphics, masks, and particle-like 2D compositions.
library_options.integration_guidance: Use a private ticker and disable autoplay with autoStart: false and sharedTicker: false; stop any already-started application. Load assets, derive scene state directly from composition time, and call app.render() explicitly on updates and seeks. Calling ticker.update() alone does not make cumulative simulation seekable.

library_options.name: GSAP
library_options.purpose: Coordinate seekable animation of DOM, SVG, and scene properties.
library_options.integration_guidance: Use the existing HyperFrames timeline contract. Animate visual layers without taking over framework-owned clip visibility or media playback. For manually drawn Canvas/WebGL scenes in HyperFrames, repaint on hf-seek as well as normal onUpdate; callback suppression during seeking must not leave stale frames.

library_options.name: Motion
library_options.runtime: browser; motion/react for mounted React components
library_options.purpose: Provide optional DOM and SVG keyframes, spring-like transitions, sequences, and staggered reveals.
library_options.integration_guidance: Use the JavaScript entry point for HTML compositions. Pause playback and set animation.time in seconds from composition time, then verify that forward, backward, and direct seeks update the visible result. Motion is an optional animation layer, not a drop-in replacement for the HyperFrames GSAP registration contract; keep the registered GSAP timeline as the framework clock and explicitly synchronize Motion. Use motion/react only within mounted React components.

library_options.name: tldraw
library_options.runtime: mounted React editor in browser; exported assets for video composition
library_options.purpose: Author diagrams, annotations, whiteboard layouts, and editable card or node artwork.
library_options.integration_guidance: Author diagrams and artwork in a mounted React editor, then export SVG or raster assets using editor.getSvgString or editor.toImage. Await export and split layers deliberately when separate animation is required; a flattened image does not preserve editable shapes. Animate those assets in the chosen framework. Verify signatures against the installed SDK; tldraw is not a video renderer or an automatic timeline adapter.

library_options.name: PhotoSwipe
library_options.runtime: browser; initialize only after the gallery DOM is mounted
library_options.purpose: Optional image-gallery dialog with swipe navigation, zoom, pan and thumbnail opening or closing transitions for interactive web delivery.
library_options.import_guidance: Use PhotoSwipeLightbox from 'photoswipe/lightbox', load 'photoswipe/style.css', and set pswpModule to () => import('photoswipe'). Check exports and API signatures against the installed version.
library_options.integration_guidance: Use for interactive image viewing only when the task includes a web gallery or lightbox. Define accurate intrinsic image dimensions and responsive sources. Retain direct image links as a fallback, meaningful image alternatives, usable keyboard navigation, focus return and reduced-motion behavior. Initialize after mounting and destroy on cleanup; access the core instance only after opening. Preserve original image colors and established palette tokens when styling controls. PhotoSwipe owns its dialog gestures and transitions; do not attach another animation owner to those properties. Captions require a deliberate custom UI or suitable plugin rather than assuming a built-in caption feature.
library_options.video_guidance: PhotoSwipe is not a video renderer or a composition-time animation engine. For rendered video, recreate the chosen thumbnail expansion, swipe, zoom, pan and reading holds as authored DOM/SVG/Canvas transforms driven by GSAP and the selected framework clock. Do not depend on live touch input, dynamic dialog state or asynchronous lightbox transitions for exported frames. Preserve HyperFrames as primary and Remotion as the existing conditional fallback.
library_options.selection_guidance: Designed primarily as an image lightbox dialog, not a general inline carousel. Use native scroll snapping or a suitable carousel library for inline cards, mixed interactive card content or persistent neighboring cards. PhotoSwipe does not generate the artwork or determine its visual style.

production_policy.principle: Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique.
production_policy.style_renderer: Owns visual construction: drawing, geometry, materials, lighting, typography, masks, textures, and specialist asset generation. Use the style-specific recommended technologies and implementation guidance.
production_policy.motion_engine: Owns trajectories, transforms, easing, transitions, deformation, and simulation. Select engines or algorithms appropriate to the action, with one owner for each animated property.
production_policy.render_pipeline: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.
production_policy.integration: Visual and motion layers expose deterministic state at composition time, or supply baked assets or frame sequences. The pipeline supplies seekable time and composes their output. Timeline registration and frame hooks are integration adapters, not substitutes for style-specific rendering or motion.
production_policy.selection: Choose only needed stack entries. A technology may serve multiple roles, but document its actual responsibility. Optional authoring, interaction, color, and preprocessing tools are not mandatory renderers or motion engines.
